outcome: Give government cio / agency operations director a governed method to improve requests resolved within statutory window using citizen requests, service taxonomy and case queues, with final decisions…
overview: Citizen Service Case Routing and SLA addresses source evidence is scattered across documents and transaction systems, leading to repeated checks and incomplete case files in government and public sector operations. The first proof of value uses citizen requests, service taxonomy and case queues. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is requests resolved within statutory window, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: citizen requests, service taxonomy and case queues; define requests resolved within statutory window and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Government CIO / Agency Operations Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including run golden documents and exceptions against the system of record.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for requests resolved within statutory window
